QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_38

question.text: FIRR (Financial Internal Rate of Return) is a return measure based on:

answer.text: The time value of money over cash flows

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 9.7 and Sample Q3: FIRR (or IRR) is based on the TIME VALUE OF MONEY applied to cash flows. Distinguished from EIRR which also considers economic benefits. The Trap: Options A, C, D ignore time-value of money. Cross-Exam Context: XXI-B and X-A/B (IA) cover IRR conceptually; XIX-C requires FIRR at fund and investor levels. Manager's Pro-Tip: Report Gross FIRR, Net FIRR (fund level), and Investor-level FIRR (post-waterfall) separately. Different LPs prioritise different metrics — sovereign wealth funds often focus on Investor-level IRR.
